proof_nodes.all_used_results_and_checks: Null sets have zero simple integral. Compare a simple minorant with c times that minorant on increasing comparison sets and use set continuity; let c increase to one and take the supremum, including infinite values. MCT gives nonnegative additivity and summable interchange. Positive/negative parts define real integration; real/imaginary parts give complex linearity. proof_nodes.all_used_results_and_checks: Apply MCT to infima of tails; compare their integrals to the corresponding infima. Apply Fatou to 2g minus the absolute difference, whose pointwise limit is 2g outside the null exceptional set. Normalization gives Cauchy-Schwarz and then Minkowski; p=1/infinity are pointwise. A summable Cauchy subsequence has an Lp majorant by MCT and a pointwise scalar limit; its tails converge in norm. Infinity uses uniform convergence off one null set. Truncation to finite-measure level sets plus finite scalar grids and DCT proves density. Scalar integration gives inner-product axioms. The general real-exponent calculus step is expressly outside this node, with the full theorem preserved.

proof_nodes.all_used_results_and_checks: Near-optimal countable cover has finite-measure union containing E and excess below epsilon. Finite truncations exhaust that union and set continuity makes the omitted tail tend to zero. Symmetric-difference error is bounded by excess plus tail; choose both below half the desired error.

proof_nodes.complete_proof_locator: Entire proof including the tower comparison and the union of all towers.
proof_nodes.hypotheses_and_scope: Every nonempty partially ordered set in which every chain has an upper bound.
proof_nodes.all_used_results_and_checks: Under no maximal element, choice selects an outside upper bound for each chain. Two towers are initial-segment comparable: the first divergence has the same predecessors and the same selected next point. The union of all towers is well ordered (choose one tower containing any given member to find the least element of a nonempty subset) and every tower is an initial segment. Adjoining its selected upper bound produces another tower and the contradiction. Only sets and choice are invoked.

proof_nodes.complete_proof_locator: Both paragraphs from the one-dimensional real functional through the final complex separation conclusion.
proof_nodes.hypotheses_and_scope: Every real or complex normed space, including nonseparable and incomplete spaces; bounded functionals separate distinct vectors.
proof_nodes.all_used_results_and_checks: For the real one-dimensional extension, every lower candidate is at most every upper candidate by the triangle inequality. Candidate zero bounds both finite endpoints, so real completeness supplies the extension value. Positive and negative scalar cases prove the norm bound. Union of a chain of compatible extensions is a valid extension; the proved Zorn lemma gives maximal full domain. In the complex case f(x)-i f(ix) is complex linear and the explicit conjugate phase proves the bound; its real value at the chosen nonzero vector is positive.

proof_nodes.complete_proof_locator: First three mathematical paragraphs before #coordinate-differential-rules; the forward smoothness remark is discharged in DIFFERENTIAL.
proof_nodes.hypotheses_and_scope: Finite real coordinate norms/matrices, orthonormalization, determinant and inverse/elementary-matrix identities, including dimension zero.
proof_nodes.all_used_results_and_checks: A squared-norm quadratic gives Cauchy-Schwarz, triangle and equivalence with maximum norm. Coordinate limits give completeness and row sums give matrix bounds and submultiplicativity. Subtracting projections gives Gram-Schmidt for an independent list. Alternating multilinear expansion proves determinant uniqueness/multiplicativity and the adjugate identities. Elimination is an induction on square matrices with zero kernel, whose remaining block has zero kernel; it reduces to identity by elementary matrices. This proves invertible iff nonzero determinant and all scaling factors.

proof_nodes.hypotheses_and_scope: Compact finite-dimensional sets, their continuous normed-space images and scalar extrema, uniform continuity, distance properties and the scalar mean-value theorem.
proof_nodes.all_used_results_and_checks: Reuse the nested-box compactness proof. Closed subsets are compact by adding the complement to covers; images by pullback of covers. Increasing bounded-value covers prove boundedness; nested closed near-supremum sets have a common point by finite-subcover contradiction, proving extrema. Finite ball covers prove compact sets closed. Triangle and infimum prove distance is Lipschitz; exterior openness and compact minima give positive separation. A finite smaller-ball cover proves uniform continuity. Interior extrema have zero derivative by the opposite one-sided signs; subtract the chord to prove the mean-value theorem.

proof_nodes.complete_proof_locator: Total differentiability definition through the finite Ck-rule paragraph, before the scalar fundamental-theorem link.
proof_nodes.hypotheses_and_scope: Finite-dimensional totally differentiable maps and bounded bilinear products; scalar reciprocal off zero; every finite Ck composition/product and smooth rational functions.
proof_nodes.all_used_results_and_checks: Differentiability implies continuity and increments O(h). Substituting two remainder formulas makes the composite remainder o(h), including zero inner increment. Bilinear expansion leaves an O(h^2) term. The exact reciprocal remainder is h^2/(z^2(z+h)); denominator control gives the derivative. Continuity and iteration of these finite formulas prove Ck rules and rational smoothness on nonzero denominator sets.

proof_nodes.complete_proof_locator: The direct continuous real scalar proof through the sentence about the scalar application, before Fix t0 in J.
proof_nodes.hypotheses_and_scope: Continuous real/complex integrands on intervals; continuously differentiable scalar functions; ordinary oriented Lebesgue integrals.
proof_nodes.all_used_results_and_checks: Continuous functions have Borel preimages, compact bounds and finite integrals on compact intervals. Additivity and the integral bound give the average-error estimate tending to zero by continuity, for either sign of h. Therefore the primitive derivative equals the integrand. Applied to u-prime, the mean-value theorem makes u minus its primitive constant. Real/imaginary or finitely many coordinate components give the stated versions. This direct scalar proof does not use vector integration, dual separation or a.e. differentiation.

proof_nodes.complete_proof_locator: Paragraph defining v and gamma through the finite-dimensional integral norm argument.
proof_nodes.hypotheses_and_scope: Every C1 finite-dimensional map on an open set and every closed segment contained in that set; induced norm bound.
proof_nodes.all_used_results_and_checks: Apply the proved chain rule to t mapped to x-prime+t v, then the scalar FTC componentwise. For a nonzero integral vector pair with its normalized direction and use scalar integration and Cauchy-Schwarz; zero integral is immediate. This proves the complete segment identity and derivative supremum bound.

proof_nodes.statement_locator: #coordinate-inverse, C1 inverse and scalar implicit formulas CI1-CI3
proof_nodes.complete_proof_locator: First four paragraphs through the C1 inverse theorem; scalar implicit paragraph and CI3, using C1 only.
proof_nodes.hypotheses_and_scope: C1 maps with invertible derivative at the point, local C1 inverse; global injective local inverses; C1 scalar implicit graphs with nonzero distinguished partial derivative.
proof_nodes.all_used_results_and_checks: Normalize derivative to identity; continuity and SEGMENT give CI1 on a closed ball. Geometric iteration constructs the unique fixed point and Lipschitz inverse. Matrix geometric series gives uniformly bounded inverse derivatives. Substitute the inverse Lipschitz increment into the first derivative remainder to prove CI2 and derivative continuity. Repeat locally for openness and patch an injective map. Apply to (p(tau,eta),eta); the block derivative is invertible and differentiating the identity gives CI3. The preserved general Holder and smooth results remain outside this C1 node pending their full scalar-power dependencies.

proof_nodes.complete_proof_locator: Entire proof from the linear-map paragraph through the absolutely integrable case, stopping before the polar-substitution paragraph.
proof_nodes.hypotheses_and_scope: Every C1 diffeomorphism between open Euclidean subsets, with every nonnegative completed-measurable integrand and every absolutely integrable complex integrand.
proof_nodes.all_used_results_and_checks: Elementary matrices and Euclidean product integration prove linear volume scaling, using one-dimensional cover scaling and translation. Cube mesh excess tends to zero, hence Lipschitz images of null sets are null locally in both directions. Normalize on a small cube; derivative uniform continuity and the segment estimate give an outer cube inclusion. The same geometric contraction proof gives inner inclusion, hence CI5. Compact support fits in finitely many interior grid cubes. Uniform oscillation bounds and null face images turn CI5 into the continuous integral formula. The explicit increasing compact continuous cutoffs prove equality on open sets. Finite bounded open exhaustions and pi-lambda uniqueness give Borel measures; local null preservation gives completions; simple approximation/MCT and complex parts give full CI4. No trigonometry, Fourier fact or polar coordinate fact is a dependency.

proof_nodes.hypotheses_and_scope: Scalar geometric and polynomial-geometric limits, absolute series products, intermediate values and continuity of monotone inverses on intervals.
proof_nodes.all_used_results_and_checks: Archimedean property follows by the supremum contradiction. Binomial lower bounds give geometric decay, and successive ratios bound polynomial factors by a larger geometric ratio. Finite geometric sums and completeness prove summability. Bisection proves intermediate values; neighboring image values prove inverse continuity. The explicit two-tail estimate controls all finite sums outside a square, hence diagonal and rectangular products have the same limit.

proof_nodes.hypotheses_and_scope: Complex exponential on the entire plane, all derivatives and addition law; real positivity, monotonicity and bijection onto positive reals.
proof_nodes.all_used_results_and_checks: Factorial ratios prove uniform absolute convergence on every disk, also after polynomial factors in the index. The exact difference-of-powers factorization controls the derivative remainder by a convergent n-squared majorant. Diagonal multiplication and the finite binomial identity prove addition and nonvanishing. Conjugation proves real values, the half-argument square proves positivity, and the derivative proves strict increase. The series lower bound and reciprocal identity prove the endpoint limits; intermediate values give the range.

proof_nodes.hypotheses_and_scope: Real logarithm on all positive reals; arbitrary real powers, their derivatives and positive-exponent extension to zero; all conjugate exponents in Young inequality; exponential decay against any real nonnegative power.
proof_nodes.all_used_results_and_checks: Continuous inverse difference quotients prove log derivative 1/x. Addition and injectivity give the logarithm law. The definition exp(a log x) gives all power identities and derivatives. Endpoint limits give continuity at zero and the needed right derivative. The derivative sign on either side of b^(1/(p-1)) proves the global minimum and Young inequality, including zero arguments. One positive term of the exponential series bounds y^M exp(-y) using an integer N>M.

proof_nodes.hypotheses_and_scope: Real sine/cosine and their addition/derivative identities; complete unit-circle parametrization; exact period and the entire complex exponential kernel.
proof_nodes.all_used_results_and_checks: Conjugate exponential formulas give real functions, derivatives, parity, addition and the circle identity. If cosine has no positive zero, increasing positive sine forces cosine negative by its integral formula. Infimum and continuity give the first zero c. Strict monotonicity covers the first quadrant exactly once; quarter rotations cover the full circle with only shared endpoints. Integer reduction proves the exact period 4c=2pi. The modulus exp(real z) identifies the entire complex kernel. The unit speed checks circumference normalization.

proof_nodes.hypotheses_and_scope: Real arctangent on the whole line, its derivative and pi/4 value, total Cauchy-kernel mass pi, and the Poisson approximate identity for bounded measurable functions continuous at the evaluation point.
proof_nodes.all_used_results_and_checks: The quotient sine/cosine on the first two neighboring quadrants is strictly increasing with infinite endpoint limits. Its inverse derivative is 1/(1+x^2). Reflection about the quarter angle gives arctan(1)=pi/4. FTC and endpoint limits give total integral pi, and monotone convergence identifies the Lebesgue integral. Comparison with t^-2 gives the explicit tail. Linear scaling proves Poisson mass one; splitting near and far proves the stated approximation for bounded measurable inputs.

proof_nodes.hypotheses_and_scope: Smooth flat functions on the real line and compact bumps, plateau cutoffs and normalized mollifiers in every positive finite Euclidean dimension.
proof_nodes.all_used_results_and_checks: Induction expresses right derivatives as finitely many inverse powers times exp(-1/t). The exponential decay estimate controls each expression and its difference quotient, proving all derivatives at zero vanish. Positivity of the displayed denominator proves smooth plateau functions. Polynomial composition gives the ball bump. Compact boundedness and a positive lower bound on a small cube prove a finite positive integral. Length/product scaling normalizes dilations. Real-power smoothness justifies the square-root normalization of finite sums.

proof_nodes.hypotheses_and_scope: Full planar polar formula for nonnegative completed-measurable functions and absolutely integrable complex functions.
proof_nodes.all_used_results_and_checks: The actual angle interval omits exactly the nonnegative horizontal ray. Circle bijectivity and the norm give global injectivity and surjectivity. The determinant is positive r; the local inverse theorem gives a global smooth inverse on the open image. The omitted ray has measure zero by countable bounded products with a singleton. Apply the previously checked completed-measurable change-of-variables theorem and the product theorem.

proof_nodes.hypotheses_and_scope: Every measure space, all 1<=p<=infinity; conjugate Holder inequality, complete norms, finite-p simple density and the L2 Hilbert conclusion.
proof_nodes.all_used_results_and_checks: Use the explicit real powers and Young proof. Normalizing and integrating gives Holder, with zero, infinite and endpoint cases treated. The elementary power bound first ensures a sum is in Lp; Holder against the (p-1)st power proves the triangle inequality. A summable-difference subsequence and monotone convergence produce the limit and tail norm estimates on any measure space. The essential-supremum proof removes only countably many measurable null sets. Truncations have finite measure support and dominated convergence; finite grid approximations give density. The already checked endpoint/L2 reasoning is preserved and uses no general-exponent circular input.

proof_nodes.hypotheses_and_scope: Local inverse and scalar implicit graph regularity for every integer k>=1 and 0<alpha<1, and smooth maps, with local uniform bounds at the stated generality.
proof_nodes.all_used_results_and_checks: Inductively differentiate DG=(DF composed with G)^-1. Matrix inversion is smooth by the proved adjugate and reciprocal rules; at derivative order j only derivatives of F up to j occur. The segment bound makes lower derivatives Lipschitz on smaller neighborhoods, with the explicit diameter conversion to alpha-Holder. Composition with a Lipschitz inverse and finite bounded products preserve Holder control; the inverse difference identity supplies its matrix factor. This yields the full kth derivative and local uniform bounds. The block inverse gives the scalar implicit formulas; every finite order gives the smooth case.

proof_nodes.hypotheses_and_scope: All C1 embedded hypersurfaces in positive finite-dimensional Euclidean spaces; chart-independent completed surface measure, C1 transitions, tangent graphs and graph Jacobians; zero-dimensional surfaces included.
proof_nodes.all_used_results_and_checks: Gram-Schmidt gives a QR factorization with positive diagonal, hence positive Gram determinant. Projection onto a tangent basis and C1 inversion construct each chart transition, with the reverse transition C1. Chain and determinant rules plus measurable substitution give chart measure compatibility. A countable chart cover from the ambient rational-ball base and disjoint Borel pieces pastes one measure; local compatibility proves cover independence and completion. Tangent projection gives the graph with zero derivative, and an orthonormal extension gives its normal component. The rank-one Gram computation gives the exact graph area factor, with the empty determinant/counting convention in dimension one.

proof_nodes.hypotheses_and_scope: Finite smooth ordinary and squared partitions near any compact subset of an open Euclidean set, global compactly supported chart weights, and a common chart for intersecting sufficiently small supports.
proof_nodes.all_used_results_and_checks: Doubled balls inside the assigned open neighborhoods and compactness give finitely many plateau bumps. Their positive sum permits ordinary normalization, and the positive square-root normalization gives squared partitions. A second compactly supported plateau construction inside the positive set gives chi=1-product(1-psi); multiplying the local normalized weights by chi extends them smoothly by zero and makes their supports compact in the charts. The maximum distance to the complements has a positive compact minimum. A set of smaller diameter meeting the compact set lies in a chart; intersecting supports of radius below delta/4 have union of diameter below delta and include a center. Empty compact sets and a full ambient chart are treated separately.

proof_nodes.hypotheses_and_scope: Every local C1 scalar submersion chart, with nonnegative completed-measurable inputs and absolutely integrable complex inputs; completed slices interpreted almost everywhere.
proof_nodes.all_used_results_and_checks: The energy map has determinant the distinguished nonzero partial derivative. The implicit derivative and rank-one Gram formula identify dS/|grad p| with the reciprocal distinguished partial times transverse Lebesgue measure. Extend the transformed function by zero off the actual image domain, then apply measurable substitution and nonnegative product integration. Completion gives almost-everywhere slices; absolute integrability and the four signed components give the complex formula.

proof_nodes.hypotheses_and_scope: p C1 on an arbitrary open Euclidean set, lambda any regular value, every compactly supported continuous complex test; no regularity of other levels is assumed.
proof_nodes.all_used_results_and_checks: On one chart the compact support stays inside the open energy-coordinate image. The transformed test times the continuous Jacobian extends continuously by zero, has support in one finite box and is uniformly continuous. Its transverse integral is therefore continuous with compact support, including the zero-dimensional transverse case. The exact Poisson approximate identity gives the local limit. For a general test, finitely many submersion patches cover the compact intersection with the regular level. Global chart weights sum to one there. The remaining compact support stays a positive energy distance from the level, giving the explicit epsilon L1/(pi delta^2) bound. Summing the finite patch limits gives the surface integral; compact local Jacobian bounds prove its finiteness. Empty support/level and zero remainder are handled explicitly.

proof_nodes.hypotheses_and_scope: Real or complex Banach spaces, without separability of the ambient space; completed Euclidean measurable domains. Smooth finite-vector density on open time intervals and completeness of L1(B).
proof_nodes.all_used_results_and_checks: Countably many approximant values have a separable closed linear span (finite rational real/complex combinations form a countable dense set). Measurable distances and nearest among the first N dense values, including zero, give a finite-valued measurable approximation with error at most the norm of f. This proves closure under almost-everywhere limits and bounded maps. Scalar dominated convergence gives L1 convergence and the nonzero-cell estimate gives finite measure. Finite interval approximation, interior truncation and the explicitly proved step cutoff give smooth finite-vector density with compact support in the time interval. A summable subsequence of a Cauchy sequence converges pointwise by Banach completeness and in L1 by the summed scalar norm tails.

proof_nodes.hypotheses_and_scope: Strongly measurable Banach-valued functions with integrable norm, arbitrary complete target Banach spaces, and norm limits on either half-line.
proof_nodes.all_used_results_and_checks: Finite intersections refine simple representations, proving linearity, norm bounds and independence. Completion extends the integral by the L1 difference estimate; the summable-subsequence argument supplies strong measurability of its L1 limits. Bounded linear maps commute with the finite sums and their limits. Scalar dominated convergence of vector norm differences gives vector dominated convergence. Tail differences form a Cauchy family, so completeness gives improper integrals with the scalar norm tail bound.

proof_nodes.hypotheses_and_scope: Scalar L1 on the line and Banach-valued L1 locally on open intervals; almost-everywhere norm Lebesgue points without an ambient separability hypothesis.
proof_nodes.all_used_results_and_checks: A finite greedy interval selection covers each compact subset of the maximal superlevel set by triple selected intervals and gives constant 3. Explicit compact exhaustion and monotone convergence give the open-set bound. Continuous scalar L1 density bounds the exceptional outer measure by 4 times the approximation error divided by epsilon; a countable epsilon union is null. Compact truncation gives the local theorem. Apply it simultaneously to countably many distances in the essential separable range; retain the factor 2, then use density. One-sided averages are bounded by twice the symmetric averages.

proof_nodes.statement_locator: #vector-primitives through (13), with the continuous scalar case at #continuous-primitives

proof_nodes.hypotheses_and_scope: Locally Bochner-integrable forcing gives a locally absolutely continuous primitive and its almost-everywhere norm derivative; continuous forcing gives an everywhere derivative; every norm-C1 function satisfies Banach FTC.
proof_nodes.all_used_results_and_checks: Truncate the scalar norm at a positive R to prove absolute continuity over small sets; disjoint increments are bounded by the norm integral of their union. Norm Lebesgue points give the difference quotient for either sign. Continuous integrands give the derivative directly by their local oscillation. For the converse C1 theorem all bounded scalar pairings of the difference have zero derivative everywhere, hence are constant by scalar MVT; the proved separation theorem gives the vector identity.

proof_nodes.hypotheses_and_scope: Continuous Banach-valued functions whose distributional derivative is locally Bochner integrable in every bounded scalar pairing; no claim that zero pointwise derivative almost everywhere suffices.
proof_nodes.all_used_results_and_checks: Absolute scalar Fubini on a compact rectangle gives the distributional derivative of a primitive with the correct sign. A normalized smooth bump is supplied by the earlier flat-cutoff proof and affine substitution. A zero-integral smooth test has a compactly supported smooth primitive inside the interval. Subtraction of a fixed integral-one test shows that each scalar pairing is a constant distribution. Explicit nonnegative point masses and the continuity bound VI2 make the equality pointwise; separation gives the vector primitive and its norm derivative.

proof_nodes.hypotheses_and_scope: Strongly continuous locally operator-norm bounded families acting on strongly measurable forcing, and locally operator-norm C1 maps between Banach spaces multiplying integrable primitives.
proof_nodes.all_used_results_and_checks: Continuous vector orbits have separable range from rational times and measurable distances. Finite-valued approximation therefore proves strong measurability of the product and its L1 bound; no operator-norm measurability is inferred from strong continuity. Continuous finite-vector approximation of the primitive derivative gives uniform approximation of the primitive. The difference quotient product rule followed by Banach FTC and L1 limits proves the integrated rule with the actual operator order. Complete graph spaces are conditional instances, and unbounded coordinate or group generators are not asserted bounded on unweighted L2.

proof_nodes.hypotheses_and_scope: Every locally operator-norm continuous generator on a real or complex Banach space, on an arbitrary open time interval. Inverse and two-time composition law hold on both sides of each initial time.
proof_nodes.all_used_results_and_checks: An operator-norm Cauchy sequence has pointwise limits with a common bound; passing linearity and the Cauchy bound to the limit proves operator-space completeness. Submultiplicativity proves continuous composition. Induction gives the factorial Picard bound for either orientation of the interval using scalar FTC. The already proved exponential series gives a uniform summable bound, operator completeness gives the continuous sum, and the integral norm inequality permits termwise passage. The continuous-integrand FTC differentiates the equation. Iterating the difference equation proves uniqueness, hence the composition law and inverse. Local inverse bounds and the exact inverse difference identity prove continuity and norm differentiability of the inverse. Uniqueness patches the finite intervals. No downstream evolution theorem is a premise.

proof_nodes.hypotheses_and_scope: Complex Banach evolution v prime equals i(Mv+h), locally norm-continuous M and locally Bochner-integrable h, with continuous distributional solution uniqueness and the precise propagator norm bound.
proof_nodes.all_used_results_and_checks: The inverse propagator times h is strongly measurable and integrable. Its primitive times the forward propagator obeys the integrated product rule and the inhomogeneous equation. Bounded maps and composition give Duhamel. Every continuous distributional solution has the primitive identity; multiplication by the C1 inverse and the inverse derivative gives the same formula, proving uniqueness. The norm integral inequality gives the stated bound with the correct time orientation.

proof_nodes.hypotheses_and_scope: Integrable primitive derivatives on either half-line, strong forcing approximation under the stated propagator bound, compact L1 families, and the nonnegative scalar first-moment identity.
proof_nodes.all_used_results_and_checks: The primitive increment is bounded by the norm tail. A time sequence tending to the end of the half-line is Cauchy, and comparison to arbitrary times proves a single strong limit with the same bound. A finite L1 epsilon cover gives one uniform tail cutoff for compact families. Scalar Tonelli on the triangular region gives the weight s-q. The receiver does not use a vector Fubini theorem or assert arbitrary completed-product interchange.

proof_nodes.hypotheses_and_scope: Real/complex complete Hilbert spaces; projection onto any closed subspace, representing vectors, bounded adjoints, finite orthogonal projections and Parseval for an already complete orthonormal family.
proof_nodes.all_used_results_and_checks: Expanding a nonnegative squared norm proves Cauchy-Schwarz. Parallelogram makes a minimizing sequence Cauchy; closedness gives the minimizer, and real/imaginary variations prove orthogonality, uniqueness, linearity and contractivity. The residual of a vector outside a closed functional kernel represents that functional; normalization gives equality of norms. Applying the representation to each target vector gives the adjoint; uniqueness and suprema give its composition and norm identities. Finite orthogonal subtraction gives Bessel, Gram-Schmidt, closed finite spans and Parseval by density. No infinite basis existence, spectral theorem or full trace-provider audit is imported.

proof_nodes.hypotheses_and_scope: Every finite Euclidean dimension with transform integral exp(-ix.xi), inverse factor (2pi)^(-n), Schwartz seminorm continuity and full forward/inverse L2 unitarity.
proof_nodes.all_used_results_and_checks: Dyadic box covers and a geometric series give integrability of negative powers beyond dimension, and exponential domination gives all Gaussian moments. Monomial expansion proves equivalence of Schwartz seminorms. Dominated difference quotients and cutoff integration by parts prove derivative identities and the exact F2 seminorm bound. The positive finite Gaussian integral is evaluated by the proved polar substitution and scalar FTC; its transform follows from the scalar differential identity with integrating factor. Gaussian regularization and two dominated limits give inversion. Absolute interchange gives Parseval. Finite-measure simple approximation, box grids and explicit flat cutoffs give Cc-infinity and Schwartz density. L2 completeness extends both mutually inverse isometries, proving surjectivity as well as norm preservation.

proof_nodes.complete_proof_locator: #tempered-fourier-duality, entire subsection F3-F4 and weighted multipliers
proof_nodes.hypotheses_and_scope: Continuous linear functionals on Schwartz seminorm space, with bilinear test pairing; all multi-index weak derivatives and all real polynomial weights.
proof_nodes.all_used_results_and_checks: The proved Schwartz continuity transposes the forward/inverse transforms to inverse maps of tempered distributions. Testing the derivative formula gives the exact D=-i partial multiplier identity. Cutoff tests converge in every Schwartz seminorm with an explicit inverse-radius bound, so compact and Schwartz test conventions agree. Cauchy-Schwarz embeds L2 continuously and injectively into the dual, and approximation in L2 proves agreement of the two Fourier transforms. Real-power differentiation and Leibniz bounds prove Schwartz continuity of each real polynomial weight and its reciprocal; transposition defines their inverse distribution multipliers.

proof_nodes.hypotheses_and_scope: All 1<=p,r,q<=infinity satisfying 1/p+1/r=1+1/q, including all endpoints, and completed-measurable representatives.
proof_nodes.all_used_results_and_checks: Scalar Young followed by normalization proves Holder; finite iteration gives the displayed factor exponents. Triangle inequalities are supplied locally and in the exact earlier Lp lemma. Borel representatives, the determinant-one joint linear substitution and the product null envelope prove measurability and almost-everywhere independence. Zero inputs are separate. The q=infinity case is Holder, q=1 is scalar Tonelli, and the remaining three-factor Holder proof gives A4 then A2 by Tonelli and increasing truncations. Zero reciprocal exponents are omitted; no interpolation theorem is used.

proof_nodes.hypotheses_and_scope: Every finite 1<=p<infinity on Euclidean space; compact smooth density and norm-continuous translations.
proof_nodes.all_used_results_and_checks: Truncate support and values, approximate finite-valued measurable functions, then approximate each level set by finite boxes. Finite endpoint grids disjointify boxes up to null faces. Explicit smooth cutoffs and dominated convergence give smooth compact approximants. Translation is an isometry by the proved measure construction; on compact smooth functions the line-segment bound and bounded support prove norm continuity. The two approximation errors and this smooth difference prove A6 for arbitrary Lp.

proof_nodes.hypotheses_and_scope: Normalized compact smooth kernels, strong approximation for finite p, smooth convolution and support control; uniform convergence for bounded uniformly continuous functions.
proof_nodes.all_used_results_and_checks: The flat bump at radius one half has compact support inside the stated unit ball. Affine substitution and probability Holder give A8, translation continuity gives pointwise-in-parameter convergence and scalar dominated convergence gives the norm limit. On compact output sets, kernel derivatives have one compact dominating support where f is L1 by Holder; difference quotients and domination give every smooth derivative. Supports add, and the uniform modulus proves the continuous statement. A radial kernel has half its mass on each side of a coordinate hyperplane; dominated continuity shows errors approaching one half on positive-measure strips. Thus the source infinity-endpoint error is not imported.

proof_nodes.hypotheses_and_scope: Every nonnegative integer k; complete Hk, equivalence with all weak derivatives through k in L2, compact smooth core, translations and compact smooth multiplication.
proof_nodes.all_used_results_and_checks: Inverse polynomial weight is at most one, so the weighted tempered definition implies an L2 transform and an L2 inverse. Multiplication of k positive polynomial factors gives exactly the finite derivative norm equivalence in both directions by F4 and Plancherel. The weighted transform is an isometric bijection onto L2, proving completeness. The tested product rule controls compact smooth multipliers. Scaled plateau cutoffs converge in every derivative norm, with positive derivative orders contributing inverse powers of the radius. Mollification commutes with every weak derivative by compact absolute Fubini and the defining test identity; finite-p norm convergence then gives the smooth compact core.

proof_nodes.hypotheses_and_scope: Riemann-Lebesgue for every L1 function and continuous compactly supported Hilbert-valued averages; symmetry-preserving averages of translated bounded Hm-to-L2 maps.
proof_nodes.all_used_results_and_checks: Smooth L1 approximation bounds Fourier error uniformly. A coordinate frequency at least |xi|/sqrt(n) and compact integration by parts give decay of the approximant. Common-refinement Riemann sums for continuous compact vector functions are Cauchy by uniform continuity and agree with the proved Bochner integral through L1 step approximation. Norm bounds and pairings pass through the limit. A11 combines Hm and L2 translation continuity with boundedness of W; integrating the actual real-weight pairing identity preserves symmetry.

proof_nodes.hypotheses_and_scope: Normalized real Gaussian packets in any positive finite dimension; L2 isometric analysis, its bounded adjoint and the exact identity resolution.
proof_nodes.all_used_results_and_checks: Gaussian normalization and Plancherel followed by nonnegative interchange prove (4). L2 density and completeness extend the isometry. Uniform Gaussian domination on compact parameter sets proves norm-continuous packet orbits and Bochner existence of the compact-support synthesis integral. Bounded pairings and absolute scalar interchange identify that integral with the adjoint. Scalar pairings of Schwartz approximants converge uniformly in parameters; an L2 almost-everywhere subsequence identifies the actual analysis representative. Expansion at u+v and u+iv proves polarization and W-star-W equals identity.

proof_nodes.hypotheses_and_scope: All smooth left symbols with derivatives through 2N separately in x and xi bounded, integer N>n/2; no ellipticity, support, positivity or Hessian assumption. Uniform families, dimension zero and every positive dilation retained.
proof_nodes.all_used_results_and_checks: For compact symbols an explicit support-volume Cauchy-Schwarz estimate proves boundedness before the packet argument. Direct substitution gives the exact constant phase and packet kernel. Separate Laplacian integrations by parts use at most 2N derivatives in each variable; all remaining polynomial-Gaussian L1 factors have the proved finite integrals. The off-diagonal bound has integrable row and column envelopes by dyadic boxes. Bochner synthesis, boundedness and pairing justify the WAW-star kernel before applying weighted Cauchy-Schwarz and Tonelli in Schur. W-star-W identity gives the original operator estimate. Fixed smooth cutoffs preserve the finite seminorm uniformly; pointwise Fourier-integral convergence and Fatou extend to every symbol, and L2 density gives uniqueness. Positive affine scaling proves the exact conjugated symbol and derivative factors.

proof_nodes.hypotheses_and_scope: Every real or complex Banach space; continuous interval and rectangle integrals, C1 fundamental theorem, chain rule, substitution and continuous partial-derivative parameter integrals.
proof_nodes.all_used_results_and_checks: Finite-cover bisection gives compactness and uniform continuity. Common refinements make tagged sums Cauchy; completeness gives the integral and norm/bounded-map/uniform-limit properties. Difference quotients prove the primitive derivative. Scalar mean values and the checked Hahn-Banach separation give the converse fundamental theorem. First-order remainder substitution proves the chain rule. Rectangular step approximations prove interchange; the fundamental theorem and joint uniform continuity prove uniform convergence of parameter difference quotients, including moving endpoints.

proof_nodes.hypotheses_and_scope: Piecewise C1 closed paths; integer and locally constant index, index one inside a circle; Goursat with one removable exceptional point, primitives and Cauchy formula on convex open subsets of C.
proof_nodes.all_used_results_and_checks: The exponential integrating factor and its checked exact kernel make the index integral an integer; the distance bound gives continuity and vanishing far out, and evaluation at the centre gives the circle index. Four-way triangle subdivision, a nested limit point and differentiability force the Goursat integral to vanish. Vertex trimming handles the exceptional point, then triangle subdivision handles all its positions. Triangle cancellation gives the segment primitive and its derivative. Applying that primitive result to the continuous difference quotient proves the Cauchy formula. Circle connectedness follows from radial segments; its exterior is joined by radial segments and arcs from the proved circle parametrization. No square-index or general-cycle theorem is imported.

proof_nodes.complete_proof_locator: Lemma 3.1, Theorem 3.2, Corollary 3.3 and Exercise 1 with complete proofs
proof_nodes.hypotheses_and_scope: Complex power series absolutely summable on smaller discs; local analyticity and Cauchy coefficient estimates, bounded entire functions, and existence of a complex root for every nonconstant polynomial.
proof_nodes.all_used_results_and_checks: On nested radii, n*q^n and n^2*q^n are bounded by a geometric tail using their eventual ratio. The exact finite difference quotient identity bounds the derivative remainder by a convergent series times |z-w|. Circle Cauchy plus the uniform geometric kernel expansion gives the coefficients and estimates; uniqueness via derivatives removes the radius dependence. Letting radius tend to infinity kills every nonconstant coefficient of a bounded entire function. A rootless polynomial has a bounded entire reciprocal because its leading term controls infinity; Liouville contradicts nonconstancy. This proves the root-existence assertion; the later unitary subsection gives the finite division identity and degree induction for full factorization.

proof_nodes.hypotheses_and_scope: Every bounded operator on a nonzero complex Hilbert space, normal norm equality, and every Laurent polynomial of an arbitrary unitary operator.
proof_nodes.all_used_results_and_checks: Pointwise limits of an operator-norm Cauchy sequence prove completeness of B(H). Norm-convergent geometric series give openness, local analytic inverses and the exterior resolvent. Scalarizing the norm-holomorphic circle formula, separation and its geometric expansion prove norm power series and derivative continuity; the finite difference-quotient bound is valid with norms. The parametrized annulus derivative is the exact t derivative of exp(it)B(R exp(it)); the checked Banach parameter theorem and periodic FTC prove radius independence. Large-circle termwise integration gives I0=I and all moments; a hypothetical empty spectrum forces I0 to vanish at small radius. Compactness gives r(T); the 2^k power norm identities follow from adjoints and normality, and moment bounds give norm=r(T). Polynomial factorization and commuting inverse identities prove exact Laurent spectral mapping, including zero factors and all constants; unitary inverse series locate its spectrum on the circle.

proof_nodes.hypotheses_and_scope: Every continuous complex function on the circle; contractive unital star homomorphism and positivity on arbitrary Hilbert spaces.
proof_nodes.all_used_results_and_checks: Finite square expansion gives positive Fejer kernels with mass 2pi; geometric sums make their off-zero mass tend to zero. Uniform continuity on the compact circle controls the near-zero integral uniformly. Finite expansion, periodic substitution and the explicit U1 coefficient formula prove each approximant Laurent. The Laurent norm inequality makes the operator limit exist independently of the approximation. The algebraic laws pass through uniform limits; the continuous positive square root and the star product prove positivity.

proof_nodes.hypotheses_and_scope: Every positive complex-linear functional on C(K), for an arbitrary compact metric space K, including the zero functional; unique finite regular Borel measure and C(K) density in L2.
proof_nodes.all_used_results_and_checks: Finite covers prove metric closedness, compact images, attained extrema, uniform continuity and positive compact-set separation. Distance cutoffs and a finite product construct subordinate functions. Positivity bounds the functional. The supremum over supported cutoffs is countably subadditive on opens; infimum over open supersets gives an outer measure. Disjoint cutoffs prove the Caratheodory splitting inequality for opens. Compact cutoff infima and support suprema prove regularity. Finite level slices squeeze the functional and integral between sums differing by m(K)/N. Outer regularity plus finite total mass proves inner regularity on all Borel sets; cutoff approximation and simple density give continuous L2 density. Monotone distance approximants determine open-set values for any finite Borel measure; the checked pi-lambda proof gives uniqueness without an extra regularity assumption.

proof_nodes.statement_locator: #unitary-cyclic-construction, entire subsection including U2 and theorem (1)
proof_nodes.complete_proof_locator: #unitary-cyclic-construction, entire subsection including U2 and theorem (1)
proof_nodes.hypotheses_and_scope: Unitary operators on Hilbert spaces of arbitrary cardinal dimension, zero space included; orthogonal strongly countably additive PVM and full bounded Borel calculus.
proof_nodes.all_used_results_and_checks: Positive vector functionals give finite measures. The exact norm identity extends continuous vectors to onto L2 isometries onto cyclic spans and intertwines U and U*. Zorn applied to the set of orthogonal cyclic reducing subspaces supplies a maximal family; its complement is reducing and cannot contain a nonzero vector. Finite Bessel sums show each vector has countably many nonzero projections and convergent squared tails; the residual is orthogonal to every summand. Indicator multiplication on each L2, followed by orthogonal direct sum, gives projections, intersection products, identity and strong countable additivity. U2 constructs the vector measure as a countable sum and proves all bounded multiplier norm/product/star laws. Dominated convergence against that finite vector measure proves bounded-pointwise strong convergence; uniform simple approximation identifies the spectral integral.

proof_nodes.hypotheses_and_scope: Every orthogonal normalized strongly countably additive Borel PVM on the circle representing the same unitary, with no separability restriction.
proof_nodes.all_used_results_and_checks: The projection sum for disjoint sets is contractive, forcing orthogonality of their ranges. Decomposing intersections gives products. Squared norms for simple multipliers give the contractive star calculus, which extends by uniform simple approximation. Laurent polynomials of either PVM equal p(U); Fejer density makes the continuous calculi coincide. All vector measures agree by compact positive-measure uniqueness; expanding diagonal quadratic forms at x+y and x+iy yields polarization and equality of every projection.

proof_nodes.hypotheses_and_scope: Norm-preserving extension from any subspace of any real/complex normed space; no completeness or closedness of the subspace required.
proof_nodes.all_used_results_and_checks: Sublinear inequalities bound the new value between a supremum and an infimum; their finite ordering and real completeness give the one-vector extension. Zorn unions preserve linearity and domination, forcing the full domain. Real seminorm domination becomes an absolute bound by negation. Extending the real part and setting F(x)=U(x)-iU(ix) proves complex linearity and agreement; rotating each value proves the seminorm bound. Restriction gives equality of operator norms.

proof_nodes.statement_locator: Complete Section3 Theorem3.1 and Section5 Theorem5.1/Corollary5.2, excluding the closed-graph theorem
proof_nodes.complete_proof_locator: Complete Section3 Theorem3.1 and Section5 Theorem5.1/Corollary5.2, excluding the closed-graph theorem
proof_nodes.hypotheses_and_scope: Baire for nonempty complete metric spaces and bounded inverse for every bounded linear bijection between Banach spaces, real or complex.
proof_nodes.all_used_results_and_checks: Nested closed balls inside successive dense open sets have radii tending geometrically to zero; completeness supplies their common limit, proving Baire and the closed-cover formulation by complements. A surjective bounded map covers its target by closures of images of growing balls. Baire supplies interior; differences and scaling give a centred ball in the closure of every scaled image. Successive lifts with geometric norm and residual bounds form a convergent series whose image is the target vector, removing the closure. Translation proves openness, and bijectivity turns its ball bound into boundedness of the inverse.

proof_nodes.hypotheses_and_scope: Finite-dimensional subspaces, closed finite-codimensional complements and Banach quotients; compactness in metric spaces and convergent subnets in compact spaces; Riesz separation in arbitrary normed spaces.
proof_nodes.all_used_results_and_checks: Closed tail closures have finite intersection property, so compactness supplies a cluster point of any net. The directed triples construction gives an increasing cofinal convergent subnet. Metric cluster points give subsequences; absence of finite epsilon nets gives a separated sequence. Total boundedness gives Cauchy subsequences; completeness and the small-ball argument for an arbitrary open cover prove compactness of the closure. Compact coefficient spheres give upper/lower norm bounds for finite-dimensional coordinates. Hahn-Banach extensions give bounded projections. Quotient Cauchy subsequences lift by summable small differences, proving quotient completeness and finite-dimensional quotient coordinates. Distance normalization proves Riesz lemma and excludes compact unit balls in infinite dimension.

proof_nodes.hypotheses_and_scope: I+C on any complex Banach space, C bounded compact; finite-dimensional kernel, closed range and a bounded inverse onto that range from any fixed closed complement.
proof_nodes.all_used_results_and_checks: C=-I on the closed kernel, so its relatively compact unit ball and Riesz lemma force finite dimension. Failure of a lower bound on a closed complement yields unit vectors with Ax_j tending to zero; compactness of Cx_j then yields a unit kernel vector in that complement, a contradiction. Replacing preimages by their complementary components and the lower bound give Cauchy convergence for every convergent image sequence. This proves closed range and the range solver including nonzero kernels.

proof_nodes.hypotheses_and_scope: Schauder compactness of the Banach adjoint and finite cokernel for I+C; no approximation property or finite-rank approximation hypothesis.
proof_nodes.all_used_results_and_checks: Pointwise limits of dual norm-Cauchy sequences are bounded functionals and converge in norm. On the compact image of the primal ball, dual unit vectors are uniformly bounded and equi-Lipschitz. Diagonal convergence at countably many finite-net points implies uniform Cauchy convergence there, hence norm convergence after C*. The proved metric compactness criterion gives compact closure. Applying the kernel proof to I+C* gives a finite-dimensional annihilator. The quotient-dual correspondence follows directly from the quotient norm. Arbitrarily many independent primal vectors yield independent extended coordinate functionals by Hahn-Banach; hence a finite-dimensional dual forces the same finite dimension of the quotient.

proof_nodes.hypotheses_and_scope: Local norm stability of the index for every Fredholm operator X to X, and zero index/invertibility criterion for every I+C compact perturbation.
proof_nodes.all_used_results_and_checks: Closed complements split kernel/range and finite-dimensional cokernel. The Banach inverse theorem bounds B0 inverse. Pointwise limit argument proves operator-space completeness; finite geometric sums give the perturbative inverse. Bounded row/column coordinate changes reduce T to T00 and its finite Schur complement, preserving closed range and defect dimensions. Finite rank-nullity gives local index equality. Every I+tC is Fredholm by preceding proofs; its norm-continuous path has locally constant index. A supremum argument on the interval forces constancy, so the identity endpoint gives zero. The complement lower bound gives the bounded inverse when the kernel is zero.

proof_nodes.hypotheses_and_scope: Strongly continuous compact-operator families over any topological parameter space with locally collectively compact images; upper kernel-dimension bound, lower bound on any fixed closed complement, locally bounded strongly continuous inverses.
proof_nodes.all_used_results_and_checks: Collective compactness bounds operator norms. If nearby kernels have larger dimension, a finite-dimensional projection onto the base kernel annihilates some unit vector in each offending kernel. A net over shrinking neighbourhoods and a compact convergent subnet converge in norm; strong continuity and uniform norms pass C_z u_z to C_0 u, contradicting the fixed complement. Adding a vanishing residual coordinate to the directed set proves the uniform lower bound by the same argument. At an invertible base point this kills the nearby kernels; zero index gives surjectivity and bounded inverses. The exact inverse-difference identity gives strong continuity and openness of the invertible set.

proof_nodes.hypotheses_and_scope: Every densely defined self-adjoint operator on any complex Hilbert space, with zero space treated separately; no lower bound.
proof_nodes.all_used_results_and_checks: Adjoint identities pass to limits and prove closedness. The exact squared norm for A plus/minus i yields injectivity and closed ranges; their orthogonal complements are the opposite deficiency kernels, hence zero. Thus both resolvents exist onto the original domain with norm at most one. Pairing proves their adjoint identity. Domain-legitimate resolvent identities give the unitary Cayley transform and trivial kernel of I-U. The checked unitary PVM and squared norm of 1-z prove its point mass at 1 is zero.

proof_nodes.hypotheses_and_scope: Normalized strongly countably additive orthogonal PVM on R and every bounded complex Borel multiplier, including the exact weighted vector-measure identity.
proof_nodes.all_used_results_and_checks: Finite rational algebra proves inverse real/punctured-circle homeomorphisms and Borel preservation. Pushing the circle PVM forward preserves products and strong sums; the omitted atom is zero. Indicators, simple approximation and monotone convergence prove the scalar pushforward integral formula. The unitary bounded calculus gives norm, star, product and bounded-pointwise strong convergence. The finite-simple-PVM proof works on the real line independently of compactness. Commuting a spectral projection through h(E) gives S1 and its nonnegative integral form.

proof_nodes.hypotheses_and_scope: Every finite-valued complex Borel function, exact maximal squared-moment domain, closedness, adjoints, ordered products and sums on their correct domains.
proof_nodes.all_used_results_and_checks: Vector-measure triangle bounds prove the moment domain linear. Bounded truncations are Cauchy there, giving linearity and the exact norm identity. S1 gives cutoff density and projection invariance. Cutoff testing of a convergent graph yields uniform truncated norms and hence closedness by monotone convergence. Testing an adjoint vector on each cutoff range proves the reverse adjoint-domain inclusion and exact adjoint. Projection norms give (7), so integrability against the new vector measure proves the exact ordered-product domain. Common bounded cutoffs give S2; their strong limit proves action equality with the inner-factor domain retained. The same argument proves the sum on the intersection, and scalar L2/L1 Cauchy-Schwarz gives the quadratic-form integral.

proof_nodes.hypotheses_and_scope: Equality with the given self-adjoint domain and action; resolvents at every nonreal z with norm bound, adjoint and exact range; uniqueness of the original PVM.
proof_nodes.all_used_results_and_checks: The bounded inverse Cayley multiplier r equals the original R+. Its weighted vector measure bounds the t moment and proves one domain inclusion and the action. Conversely r(E)(T_t+i)u=u places every maximal t-moment vector in the original resolvent range. For nonreal z, bounds on r_z and t r_z make both inverse products legitimate and prove S3 with range exactly D(A). A second PVM with the same domain/action yields the same inverse r(G), hence the same Cayley unitary. Its pushforward has zero omitted atom and equals the original circle PVM by the checked uniqueness theorem; the homeomorphism gives equality on R.

proof_nodes.hypotheses_and_scope: Strongly continuous unitary group with generator domain exactly D(A), every positive integer power with maximal moment domain, and support specialization for any actual lower bound.
proof_nodes.all_used_results_and_checks: Bounded multiplicativity proves the unitary group law, and finite vector-measure dominated convergence proves continuity. The scalar FTC writes the exponential difference quotient as it times a unit-modulus average; domination by t squared yields the derivative on D(A). A strong derivative implies bounded quotient norms; Fatou forces the same second moment, giving the converse. Ordered products and lower-moment domination prove every power-domain equality. On bounded spectral intervals below a lower bound, the already proved quadratic-form integral contradicts positivity unless the projection vanishes; countably many such intervals exhaust the forbidden half-line.

proof_nodes.hypotheses_and_scope: Every bounded open subset of R^n, n at least one, zero-boundary energy space defined by closure; Poincare, zero extension, completeness and compact inclusion. Boundary smoothness is not used in this scope.
proof_nodes.all_used_results_and_checks: Linewise scalar FTC and Cauchy-Schwarz give Poincare with 2R. L2 convergence tested against compact smooth functions proves the zero-extension derivative rule and completeness. Plancherel and the exact weak Fourier derivative give the high-frequency estimate. Finite simple approximation and Euclidean rectangles give product-kernel L2 density; Cauchy-Schwarz bounds each kernel operator and each error, while product kernels have finite rank. Approximate the frequency ball indicator by compact smooth multipliers: absolute Fourier interchange on compact smooth input and L2 limits prove the asserted convolution kernel, with both unitary constants retained. Truncation inside Q and mollification prove input density. Finite-dimensional compactness, finite nets and target completeness prove compactness of the two successive operator-norm limits.

proof_nodes.hypotheses_and_scope: Bounded compact positive injective self-adjoint inverse K on L2, with range dense and bounded into H_0^1, for any bounded open set.
proof_nodes.all_used_results_and_checks: The energy inner product is complete by Poincare and Section1. The parallelogram projection argument and the correctly conjugate-linear functional representation yield a unique weak solution. Testing it against itself proves both inverse bounds. Pairing two solutions proves bounded self-adjointness and positivity. Truncation away from the closed complement followed by mollification proves compact-test L2 density, so the kernel is zero. Orthogonal complement and adjoint identities give dense range.

proof_nodes.hypotheses_and_scope: Signed discrete integration by parts, weak derivative commutation, coefficient product rule, derivative bound on valid shifted patches and L2 weak-derivative converse.
proof_nodes.all_used_results_and_checks: Change of variables against the shifted compact test proves derivative commutation and the exact backward-quotient negative sign. Scalar FTC, Cauchy-Schwarz and Fubini bound a smooth quotient by the intervening derivative norm; H1 approximation passes to each function used. Conversely testing uniformly bounded quotients gives a bounded conjugate-linear functional on compact smooth L2 tests. Extend by density, apply the proved Hilbert representation and retain the minus sign to identify the weak derivative and its bound. No weak sequential compactness theorem is assumed.

proof_nodes.hypotheses_and_scope: Every weak H_0^1 solution of minus Delta u=f in L2 on a bounded smooth open set, n at least one, has the full H2 estimate; disconnected sets allowed.
proof_nodes.all_used_results_and_checks: The distribution equation extends to all energy tests and gives the first-derivative bound. Smooth boundary means local graph charts; their explicit inverse and compact subpatch bounds yield a uniformly positive smooth real matrix JBB^T in the weak form. Pullbacks of H_0^1 approximants prove the weak chain rule and the admissibility of tangential difference tests without a trace converse. Expand every error term: coefficient differences and cutoff derivatives are bounded, while the principal elliptic term controls X_h squared. Cauchy-Schwarz and elementary epsilon absorption give a uniform quotient bound, hence all tangential second derivatives. The distribution equation and A_nn at least theta give the remaining normal derivative, also when n=1. Interior mollification and the finite chain rule identify the exact second-derivative pullback on compact subpatches; uniform bounds extend it to the full smaller patch. Finite boundary and interior covers plus matching distributions on overlaps give the global estimate. The initial energy bound replaces the H1 term.

proof_nodes.hypotheses_and_scope: Continuous local H1 trace on the smooth boundary and zero trace of every H_0^1 function; only this implication is claimed.
proof_nodes.all_used_results_and_checks: Integrate the derivative of the squared modulus, average the upper endpoint and use Fubini and Cauchy-Schwarz to obtain the finite-strip trace bound. Shift toward the interior and mollify at a smaller radius; zero extensions are used only for L2 translation comparisons, not as weak Sobolev extensions. This proves smooth approximation up to the flat face and hence a unique continuous restriction map. Smooth coordinate and surface-density bounds transfer the estimate. The original compact interior approximants have zero trace and pass to the H1 limit. No omitted converse from Hunter is invoked.

proof_nodes.hypotheses_and_scope: The positive self-adjoint Dirichlet Laplacian with domain exactly H2 intersect H_0^1, graph-norm equivalence, bounded compact inverse and every nonreal resolvent compact.
proof_nodes.all_used_results_and_checks: Set A=K inverse on its dense original range. proof_nodes.all_used_results_and_checks: Distance to the closed complement is continuous, with empty complement interpreted as infinity. The compact K_m exhaust O and lie in interior K_(m+1). Each band K_m minus interior K_(m-1) is compact, disjoint from K_(m-2), and inside interior K_(m+1). Positive distances permit finitely many smaller balls with doubled closures in both the assigned cover member and the larger open band. Smooth bumps positive on the smaller balls cover the band. Every point has a neighborhood inside some K_M, while all sufficiently late supports avoid K_M. Thus the countable family is locally finite, its sum positive smooth, and division gives a subordinate partition. Empty O is vacuous.

proof_nodes.statement_locator: #distorted-polynomial-null, polynomial zero-set proof in the end of Lemma 2.1
proof_nodes.complete_proof_locator: #distorted-polynomial-null, polynomial zero-set proof in the end of Lemma 2.1
proof_nodes.hypotheses_and_scope: Every nonzero real polynomial in any positive finite dimension; all individual levels of nonconstant p and the countable exceptional preimage.
proof_nodes.all_used_results_and_checks: The monomial difference identity factors t-a at a root. Degree induction gives at most d roots in one variable, with the nonzero constant case empty. In higher dimension choose a nonzero coefficient polynomial in the last variable; dimension induction makes its zero set in the other variables null. Away from that set every section has finitely many roots. Within a bounded box the exceptional sections have uniformly bounded length and all other zero-set sections have zero length; the zero-set indicator is Borel, so Tonelli gives zero volume. Countably many boxes cover space. Each p-lambda is nonzero by nonconstancy, so countability of Sigma makes its entire preimage null.

proof_nodes.hypotheses_and_scope: Each f in B, both signs, jointly Borel ambient representative with canonical trace at every good energy, arbitrary noncompact or disconnected shells and dimension one.
proof_nodes.all_used_results_and_checks: Schwartz density in B followed by smooth compact Fourier truncation proves density of inverse Fourier Cc-infinity. Fourier-Schwartz continuity and the explicit dyadic bound with exponent (n+1)/2-N<0 give B convergence. Cover parameter space by neighborhoods of fixed approximants and use the locally finite partition, so h_j has B error <=2^-j everywhere and compact smooth Fourier support at each parameter. G_j(xi)=Fh_j(p(xi))(xi) is locally a finite sum of continuous terms, hence Borel. At each fixed energy uniform local trace bounds make successive L2(dS) errors summable. Monotone convergence of squared sums of absolute differences gives pointwise convergence outside a surface-null set, and the L2 limit is the canonical trace. The countable Cauchy criterion makes the convergence set Borel; define the limit there and zero elsewhere. The local inverse energy Jacobian is 1/|partial_1p| and the graph Gram factor gives exactly dS/g. Patching and increasing compact cutoffs prove full nonnegative coarea. Every-energy surface-null differences give an ambient null set, and the countable polynomial preimage is null. This proves uniqueness without taking arbitrary ambient L2 representatives on the diagonal.

proof_nodes.statement_locator: #distorted-norm, Theorem 3.1 through bounded extension and the norm identity
proof_nodes.complete_proof_locator: #distorted-norm, Theorem 3.1 through bounded extension and the norm identity
proof_nodes.hypotheses_and_scope: All B vectors and then all L2 vectors; norm exactly that of E(Omega)f, both signs, no surjectivity assumption.
proof_nodes.all_used_results_and_checks: Increasing compact continuous cutoffs exist by radial and distance-to-Sigma cutoffs; their factors may be chosen monotone, vanish near Sigma and tend to one on Omega. Monotone convergence of the density identity and coarea gives ||Jf||^2=||Ecf||^2. At every good shell canonical traces of linear combinations agree; coarea and ambient uniqueness give L2 linearity. The norm bound one extends from dense B uniquely. Passing to L2 limits preserves the equality and shows that the transform vanishes on Ed and is an isometry on Ec. This proves closed isometric range only, retaining the later separate onto question.

proof_nodes.statement_locator: #distorted-spectral-parts, full atomic and absolutely continuous decomposition
proof_nodes.complete_proof_locator: #distorted-spectral-parts, full atomic and absolutely continuous decomposition
proof_nodes.hypotheses_and_scope: All threshold eigenspaces allowed with arbitrary multiplicity; full L2 pure point span and absolutely continuous subspace; absence of singular continuous spectrum.
proof_nodes.all_used_results_and_checks: A point-projection vector has finite second moment and zero (H-lambda) norm; conversely that norm zero forces spectral measure onto the point. Countable strong additivity over Sigma gives exactly the closed sum of these orthogonal eigenspaces. U014 places every nonthreshold eigenvalue in A; threshold values already lie in Sigma. For a Borel null set in Omega, the continuous density annihilates every B test and bounded projections plus density give E(N)=0 on all L2. Vectors in Ec therefore have absolutely continuous measures on all R. Conversely an absolutely continuous measure vanishes on the countable set Sigma, so Ed kills the vector. Measures on Ed are countable atom sums, and the two reducing orthogonal parts exhaust L2. No threshold decay or finite multiplicity assumption is introduced.

proof_nodes.hypotheses_and_scope: The original Schwartz core of the rough differential self-adjoint closure; both signs and every good energy.
proof_nodes.all_used_results_and_checks: The Schwartz polynomial image belongs to B, as does Vphi by the compact extension from Xp, so Hphi and (H-lambda)phi are valid B forcing terms. The nonreal identity R0(z)(P0-lambda)phi=phi+(z-lambda)R0(z)phi passes to each regular boundary using endpoint bounds, giving exactly phi. Hence (H-lambda)phi=(I+VR0)(P0-lambda)phi. Inverting the good-energy factor and taking the canonical trace yields zero because (p-lambda)Fphi restricts to zero. Linearity at each fixed energy, followed by coarea, gives JHphi=pJphi almost everywhere. The left side is L2, proving maximal multiplication-domain membership on the core.

proof_nodes.statement_locator: #distorted-domain and #distorted-group, full closure and time-group proof
proof_nodes.complete_proof_locator: #distorted-domain and #distorted-group, full closure and time-group proof
proof_nodes.hypotheses_and_scope: Every vector in the exact original D(H) for operator intertwining and every L2 vector for all real times; abstract bounded intertwiner between arbitrary self-adjoint Hilbert-space operators in Solution 5.5.
proof_nodes.all_used_results_and_checks: Graph-core approximation and boundedness of J give convergent transformed inputs and operator outputs. Multiplication is closed: a common subsequence with summable squared L2 errors converges in both entries almost everywhere by Tonelli, identifying the output as p times the input. Thus full domain intertwining follows. Spectral second moments prove group domain invariance and strong differentiability, with difference quotient bounded by |lambda| and dominated square convergence. For y(t)=Je^(itH)f, y is differentiable, lies in D(Mp), and Mp y(t)=Je^(itH)Hf is continuous. Splitting the product difference quotient into varying y and fixed domain vector terms gives derivative e^(-itMp)(yprime-iMp y)=0. Scalar pairings and the continuous primitive theorem give constancy. Dense-domain approximation extends to all vectors. The abstract solution supplies the same exact argument without separability or a special multiplier representation.

proof_nodes.hypotheses_and_scope: Free one-dimensional square at all nonzero energies and all L2 vectors, exact two-branch density; the actual sech bound state at -1 and its trace at every good energy.
proof_nodes.all_used_results_and_checks: With V0, forcing correction is identity; on Schwartz vectors the every-energy trace equals the ordinary Fourier value. The exceptional polynomial preimage is null, so J=Fourier in ambient L2; boundedness and density give equality on all L2. At lambda>0 the two points each have counting measure one and g=2sqrt(lambda), giving exact equation19; negative shells are empty. Sech is an actual domain eigenfunction by U014. Its exponential bound also gives B membership, since each one-dimensional shell term <=C R_j exp(-R_j/2)<=C R_j^-2 by the exponential series. Norm equality kills J; continuity and nonnegativity of its density make it zero at every good energy, and positive finite g on countable compact surface patches gives trace zero there. No onto theorem is presumed.

proof_nodes.hypotheses_and_scope: Both signs; all (lambda,t) in Omega times R, including arbitrary noncompact or disconnected shells and dimension one; each fixed-time ambient L2 class.

proof_nodes.complete_proof_locator: #completeness-fubini, the entire time/surface interchange through equation 12

Positive minimum g on a compact regular patch and coarea give the same ambient L2 bound. For a general jointly measurable F with integral L2 norm M, Tonelli and finite patch volume give scalar absolute integration. Pairing against q in L2 is absolutely integrable by Cauchy-Schwarz. Testing the resulting h with truncated h establishes h in L2, norm<=M, before using L2 duality to identify the norm integral. proof_nodes.hypotheses_and_scope: JW=Fourier on all L2 for each matching sign, full rough differential hypotheses and exceptional thresholds, with no prior surjectivity.
proof_nodes.all_used_results_and_checks: The damped Cook vectors converge globally in L2 by the known L2 time majorant. J and group intertwining transfer that limit. At each good energy the strong B boundary limit and inverse cancellation make the assembled trace tend to Tf. On every compact frequency subset of p^-1(Omega), energies have a finite compact interval cover, all endpoint graph and trace norms are uniform, and g has a positive minimum. Coarea and dominated convergence give local L2 convergence of the same representatives to Fourier f. The global and local limits agree. Countable exhaustion and the previously proved null preimage of countable Sigma give global equality. Dense packets and bounded J,W,Fourier extend it to all L2. No pointwise limit is inferred from a bare L2 limit.

proof_nodes.hypotheses_and_scope: Both wave operators onto the complete absolutely continuous perturbed subspace and both stationary transforms onto Fourier L2; full scattering unitary and its exact transform identity.
proof_nodes.all_used_results_and_checks: JW=Fourier onto first makes J onto. For any u in Ec choose f=Fourier^-1 Ju; J(Wf-u)=0 and injectivity on Ec imply Wf=u. Isometries onto the common closed range satisfy W*W=I and WW*=Ec. Direct multiplication gives S*S=SS*=I. Group intertwining and its adjoint give free group commutation. On the common range Fourier W+*=J+ and W- Fourier^-1=J-^-1; composing proves formula17 with inverse restricted to Ec. No onto assertion is borrowed from a stationary source.

proof_nodes.hypotheses_and_scope: Every Borel energy region and exact maximal operator domains, all threshold eigenspaces with any multiplicity; no claim to an individual-fiber scattering operator yet.
proof_nodes.all_used_results_and_checks: S is now an isometric group intertwiner, so the earlier damped scalar resolvent/spectral-measure proof gives equal projection norms for S f and f. Polarization gives S*E(A)S=E(A); surjectivity gives SE(A)=E(A)S. Thus both S and its inverse preserve every energy region, and multiplication by its p-preimage gives the momentum version. Differentiating the unitary group identity gives W D(H0) contained in D(H)capEc; applying the inverse unitary to a domain orbit gives the reverse inclusion by the proved spectral generator criterion. The orthogonal part is the closed span of all bound states from U015, including thresholds, without new decay or finite-dimensional assumptions.

proof_nodes.hypotheses_and_scope: Every bounded real multiplication potential under C/((1+r)log(e+r)^2), especially Laplacian in arbitrary positive finite dimension; no replacement by a power-decay subcase.
proof_nodes.all_used_results_and_checks: U013 proves the actual decreasing integrable logarithmic envelope, exact local shell summability and strict weakness of the constant multiplier relative to proper tilde-p. It also proves slower decay than every stronger fixed power. For p=|xi|^2, the sum of all squared polynomial derivatives is |xi|^4+4|xi|^2+4n, bounded by C(1+|xi|^2)^2, which supplies the simply characteristic inequality including its constant term. The t^2 coefficient in translation by tv is |v|^2, excluding invariant directions. Full completeness therefore applies without strengthening the stated envelope.

proof_nodes.hypotheses_and_scope: Whenever the declared boundary products are defined, H=H0+V and R0=(H0-z)^-1; both adjoint boundaries with correct convention.
proof_nodes.all_used_results_and_checks: Applying H0-lambda to psi0-R0+Vpsi gives -Vpsi, the required equation. The opposite sign gives +Vpsi. Multiplying the correctly rearranged equation by V gives (I+VR0+)Vpsi=Vpsi0, so the forcing inverse has a plus although the eigenfunction equation has a minus. Taking adjoints exchanges half-planes without changing V. This is an algebraic implication under defined products; the next explicit example proves that the wrong sign has genuinely nonzero residual.

proof_nodes.complete_proof_locator: #completeness-green-kernel, upper boundary kernel and exact domain identification

proof_nodes.all_used_results_and_checks: Explicit positive a_epsilon,b_epsilon give kappa^2=1+i epsilon and kappa->1. The exponentially decaying G_epsilon is L1capL2 and has derivative jump -1, hence (-d2-z)G=delta, as integration by parts on the two half-lines shows. Young gives G*h in L2; its distributional second derivative is -zv-h in L2. Plancherel then gives maximal H2 membership. Nonreal self-adjoint uniqueness identifies the actual resolvent. Compact bounded h belongs to B and L1; locally uniform kernel convergence gives locally uniform convolution convergence. The free endpoint theorem gives distributional resolvent convergence, so uniqueness identifies R0+ h=G*h. Smooth-flat-cutoff and bounded perturbation proofs give the potential and H2 realization.

The norm Neumann series has explicit geometric tail and multiplying finite partial sums by I+K proves the inverse. It yields sup error<=1/7 and modulus>=6/7. The global kernel formula restricts to the constructed interval solution and gives the distributional equation. A continuous RHS has a twice-integrated C2 primitive. A zero-derivative distribution is constant because every zero-integral test has a compact primitive; applying this twice proves the remaining distribution affine. Bootstrapping psi-second=(V-1)psi gives smoothness.
