All five bodies and all 29 original displayed equations are byte-identical.

proof_nodes.hypotheses_and_scope: Every regular energy for a real simply characteristic p without invariant directions and rough symmetric short-range V; arbitrary noncompact or empty shells, unbounded g, both labels and full Xp.
proof_nodes.all_used_results_and_checks: The energy extension has density b/g. Threshold bounds control every derivative-of-p multiplier divided by g, so each graph component is the bounded surface extension of an L2 density. Conversely the homogeneous classification applies to each graph component; summing the n gradient norms gives ||gv||2<=C||u||Xp. This gives an isomorphism with unweighted amplitudes without assuming g bounded above. Applying the forced theorem to -Vu gives unique opposite-boundary homogeneous additions; its jump yields bplus-bminus=-2pi i TVu. Extended symmetry makes the flux imaginary part zero. Dividing surface densities by g yields exact equality of the two physical norms, both finite since 1/g is bounded. Empty shells give zero homogeneous space.

proof_nodes.hypotheses_and_scope: Every good energy and every B forcing, paired with every stationary Xp solution; exact unitary Fourier normalization and linear-first convention.
proof_nodes.all_used_results_and_checks: The canonical transform is the trace of the inverted B forcing h. Extension duality with b/g gives the physical pairing as (h,uplus/minus). Inserting the opposite-boundary addition and conjugate free boundary adjointness moves R0 to h with the matching sign. Extended V symmetry moves V and the inverted forcing identity gives (f,u). All pairings are B/Bstar pairings and are finite. Free adjointness follows from nonreal adjointness and weak-star limits against fixed B elements, so no unproved trace of an ambient representative or extra Fourier constant is used.

proof_nodes.hypotheses_and_scope: All regular energies, including point spectrum; exact entire L2 eigenspace, finite dimension, rapid decay and actual closed operator domain; general Banach Xp.
proof_nodes.all_used_results_and_checks: Aplus kernel gives one zero amplitude, flux gives the other, proving equal kernels. The earlier rapid/domain theorem puts them in D(H), and the whole-eigenfunction theorem supplies the converse. Bounded free boundary after compact V makes R0V compact; the general Banach Fredholm proof gives closed range and index zero. V is injective on the kernel by the boundary equation. Opposite-boundary adjointness and V symmetry annihilate the range against every Vw. These r functionals are independent by compact smooth testing and V injectivity. Their joint kernel has codimension r by finite-dimensional linear algebra, so containment and equality of codimension give the exact range. No representation of the full Banach dual by B functions is assumed.

proof_nodes.hypotheses_and_scope: Every unweighted L2 incoming or outgoing amplitude at any regular energy, including eigenvalues; a bounded linear range solver chosen on a closed complement.
proof_nodes.all_used_results_and_checks: For each kernel vector the two free boundaries agree, so the injective jump/zero-trace criterion gives TVw=0. Extension duality annihilates the free incoming wave against Vw, giving exact Fredholm solvability. Two solutions differ in the common kernel and hence have identical outgoing amplitudes. Reversing signs gives the inverse amplitude map. Continuous finite-dimensional coordinates and Hahn-Banach extensions give a bounded kernel projection. On its closed complement, a failed inverse norm bound would yield unit yj with Ayj->0 and compact Cyj convergent, hence a unit vector in the zero intersection. This proves the bounded range solver. The difference S-I=-2pi i TVGE factors through compact V and bounded maps, so is compact; the reverse solver bounds S inverse. All signs follow the unchanged opposite-boundary amplitude labels.

proof_nodes.hypotheses_and_scope: Every exponent kappa from zero through two, with compatible compact extensions and inverse on each space, physical unitarity at one; weight may approach zero.
proof_nodes.all_used_results_and_checks: The weight a=1/g is positive bounded continuous on the regular shell, with no required positive infimum. Unweighted S-I is compact and the flux identity gives ||Sb||a=||b||a on the unweighted dense domain. Every hypothesis of the complete U017 theorem is therefore met; its weighted adjoint, compatible second endpoint, cutoff compactness and three-lines proof give exactly the whole closed interval of exponents and unitarity in the middle. Empty shells are zero spaces. No norm continuity in energy or stronger decay assumption is added.

proof_nodes.hypotheses_and_scope: Every momentum L2 input, physical weighted fiber action at almost every energy; canonical B traces at every good energy, no prior measurable operator-field assumption.
proof_nodes.all_used_results_and_checks: The two exact stationary pairings show (Jplus f,Sb)=(Jminus f,b). Unitarity and explicit density via 1_{g<=N}h give Jplus f=S Jminus f at every good energy. Onto Jminus and dense B give global approximants with summable L2 errors, and Q unitarity gives the same for outputs. Coarea and scalar L2 triangle bound every partial sum of fiber error norms; monotone convergence bounds the infinite sum, so both errors tend to zero in fiber norm outside one null set. Countably many canonical representative identifications can share this null set. Fiber unitarity passes the pointwise equality to the limit. Countable Sigma and its polynomial preimage are null. The resulting Qh supplies the measurable representative, while coarea identifies representatives on almost all fibers and proves independence. The claim is not promoted to every-energy evaluation of arbitrary ambient L2 inputs.

proof_nodes.hypotheses_and_scope: Any regular-energy bound-state ambiguity, with the explicit one-dimensional negative-energy example and zero amplitude spaces.

The earlier exact H2 example H=-d2-2sech^2 has actual eigenfunction sech at -1. This energy is regular for the free square, with empty real shell. Its nonzero eigenkernel coexists with the unique identity on zero amplitude space, so no uniqueness of the interior stationary solution is falsely inferred.

proof_nodes.hypotheses_and_scope: Every L2 sphere amplitude, exact unitary Fourier convention at d3,lambda1,g2; actual graph-space averaged solution and smooth bounded kernel.
proof_nodes.all_used_results_and_checks: The free energy extension has coefficient1/[2(2pi)^(3/2)]. Finite sphere area makes each L2 amplitude L1. The continuous bounded C(ball)-valued solution family times b is strongly measurable and norm integrable; the Banach integral allows bounded inverse and point evaluations through. Scalar Fubini for compact spatial convolution uses locally integrable1/r and uniform solution bounds. Thus the average has the same integral equation, free term in Xp and bounded compact forcing in B; R0+ supplies the remaining Xp term. Applying the exact amplitude jump gives kernel -i kappa J/(8pi^2). Constant1/sqrt2 conversion to the usual sphere Hilbert norm leaves the kernel unchanged. The elementary difference-of-squares identity gives |r omega-y|=r-omega.y+O(1/r) uniformly for |y|<=1, and reciprocal/phase bounds give G=e^ir e^-iomega.y/(4pi r)+O(r^-2). Integrating proves outgoing amplitude -kappa J/(4pi), consistent with the stated normalization. These steps avoid integrating individual plane waves as Xp-valued objects.

proof_nodes.hypotheses_and_scope: Explicit compact smooth potential satisfying all rho4 derivative bounds in d3, actual smooth kernel and positive lower bound on off-diagonal neighborhoods.
proof_nodes.all_used_results_and_checks: Exponential difference <=|omega-omegaprime| on the unit ball and the uniform1/7 solution error give |J-Iw|<=Iw(1/7+delta). For0<delta<=1/7, |J|>=5Iw/7 and hence |k|>=5kappa Iw/(56pi^2). The global bound ||psi||<=8/7 gives |k|<=kappa Iw/(7pi^2); compact integration with the proved incident derivatives gives smoothness in both directions. Any putative C delta bound contradicts the lower bound on a nonempty open set of pairs with delta sufficiently small. Positive chart Jacobians give that set positive product measure, so changing a representative on a null set cannot fix the inequality. No general substitute decay-exponent theorem is asserted.

proof_nodes.hypotheses_and_scope: Arbitrary physical shell Hilbert space; spectrum on unit circle, finite multiplicity and no accumulation away from one; unrestricted multiplicity at one.
proof_nodes.all_used_results_and_checks: For V0, S=I; disjoint positive-measure spherical annuli give infinitely many orthogonal eigenvectors at one. Neumann series invert S-s outside the unit circle, using S inverse=S* inside it. For s different from one, identity plus scaled compact factor and the compact alternative show every noninvertible value is an eigenvalue. On that eigenspace K=(s-1)I, so infinite orthonormal sequences contradict compactness. Unitarity makes distinct eigenvectors orthogonal. Infinitely many distinct eigenvalues bounded away from one would give pairwise separated compact images of normalized eigenvectors, impossible.
